name: r2-surprises-2
statement: Which entries the RL-Zero update moves, and by how much each, is set by the base and the optimizer rather than by the task (Adam gives every consistently signed coordinate a near-equal step, and bf16 storage registers a step only where it exceeds half an ulp of |w|), so the changed-entry mask and entry magnitudes carry almost no task information; the task is written only in the signs, and their effect is gated by which input directions the processed text excites, so RL changes the computation on any math-solution text whoever wrote it and leaves general text untouched.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math (step 2,800) and Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code, all 2-D weight matrices; weight statistics, teacher-forced activations, and MATH-500 accuracy of edited deltas at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, grader v3. It does not cover supervised fine-tune deltas (large enough that every entry moves past its ulp), sampling settings, the cue, or the residual accuracy gap. Parent r1-surprises-2 (low-rank function, high-rank optimizer noise) is revised because result-c9b27e shows Math-RL and Code-RL share their changed entries 1.64x above chance with chance-level sign agreement, and knowledge-87618d shows divergence equal on base-written and RL-written math text: the first needs a base-set mask, the second an input-gated effect, neither of which a low-rank account supplies.

explains.quote: Both change the same entries 1.64x more than chance
explains.how: The mask is fixed by the base's |w| (bf16 ulp) and the optimizer, so two RL runs on different data register changes on the same entries.
Signs carry the task, so on the shared entries Math-RL and Code-RL agree in sign only at chance.
Most registered changes are one quantum of storage: entry size is a readout of bf16 resolution, not of importance.
Sub-ulp Adam steps leave over half the entries bit-equal, whereas a large supervised delta moves nearly every entry.

explains.quote: 52 of 805,306,368 body MLP entries are bit-equal
explains.how: The SFT delta's steps exceed the ulp almost everywhere, so its mask is complete; the partial RL mask is a storage threshold effect.
Overall direction cosine is near zero because signs on the shared mask are nearly independent; the small excess is the shared deliberation readout.

explains.quote: Weight change is flat: each layer 3.0-3.2 % of the MLP change
explains.how: Adam's near-equal per-entry steps spread change energy evenly over layers, whatever each layer's functional role.

explains.quote: random neurons matched on change energy (two kinds) 58.0-63.8: H_local REFUTED
explains.how: Ranking by change magnitude ranks by optimizer and storage artefacts, so the top-changed neurons are no better than random ones.
Attribution weights each signed change by the activation that passes through it (13.7 / 18.6 %), the quantity that carries effect; magnitude alone recovers a third of that.

explains.quote: yet it scores like the whole MLP delta
explains.how: DARE keeps each surviving entry's sign, and signs are where the task lives, so a 1 % sign-preserving sample rescaled works like the whole delta.

explains.quote: So the drop is not specific to text RL wrote.
explains.how: The signed change acts on input directions that any math solution excites, so base-written and RL-written solutions diverge equally.
General text does not excite the input directions the signed change sits on, so activations are unchanged there.

explains.quote: RL barely moves which tokens a neuron fires on most
explains.how: On a general corpus the update is gated off, so neurons' top contexts stay at noise level.

conflicts.quote: 11.8% of its squared norm sits in 8 singular directions per matrix
conflicts.how: The delta's magnitudes have low-rank structure 15-20x above a Gaussian null, so magnitudes carry some structure beyond storage and optimizer artefacts; the theory must hold that this structure comes from sign coherence across rows and columns, not from entry sizes.

conflicts.quote: the 131 and 1,311 most-changed neurons with F's values give 22.67 and 20.00
conflicts.how: For the SFT delta, whose magnitudes are not ulp-limited, magnitude ranking also fails, so magnitude uninformativeness may not be due to bf16 and Adam alone.
RL does shift general-corpus top contexts above the noise floor, so the gating off general text is not complete.

conflicts.quote: MLP layers 0-15 carry about twice what 16-31 do
conflicts.how: KL closure is uneven over layers while change energy is flat, consistent with input gating, but activation divergence grows with depth (knowledge-87618d), the opposite layer order; input gating alone does not say why.

rival: r1-surprises-2: function lives in a few coherent singular directions per matrix and the high-rank remainder is noise. Separation: replace every changed entry's magnitude with its matrix's mean |change| while keeping signs; this theory predicts near-RL accuracy (magnitudes carry no task information), while the low-rank rival predicts a large loss because flattening magnitudes destroys the low-rank head (most of the sign-only delta's energy becomes high-rank). Second separator: the Math/Code shared-entry excess conditioned on |w| deciles; this theory predicts it nearly vanishes, the rival says nothing about the mask.

predictions.experiment: Base + sign-only RL-Math delta (each changed entry set to sign(delta) x its matrix's mean |delta| over changed entries, unchanged entries left at base), all 2-D matrices, plain prompt, MATH-500 n=500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, grader v3 (endpoints v3: base 305, RL 464)
predictions.refuted_by: fewer than 410 right: entry magnitudes carry task information that signs alone do not

predictions.experiment: Weights only: Math-RL vs Code-RL co-change ratio (entries changed in both / expected under independence) computed within deciles of base |w| per tensor, then averaged weighted by entry count (pooled value 1.64)
predictions.refuted_by: within-decile ratio 1.40 or above: the shared mask is not a readout of the base's |w|

predictions.experiment: Weights only: fraction of entries changed by RL-Math in the smallest base-|w| decile divided by the fraction changed in the largest decile, pooled over all 2-D matrices
predictions.refuted_by: ratio 1.2 or below: registration of a change does not depend on bf16 resolution

predictions.experiment: knowledge-87618d protocol (per-neuron Pearson r of mlp.down_proj inputs, base vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math) on the 500 MATH-500 problem statements alone, no solution text: median r in layers 24-31
predictions.refuted_by: median r 0.95 or below: math notation alone, not solution text, gates the change

predictions.experiment: knowledge-87618d protocol with Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code vs base, on the base's own 500 MATH-500 answers: median r in layers 24-31 (Math-RL gives 0.920 on the same text)
predictions.refuted_by: median r 0.93 or below: any RL decorrelates math text as much as Math-RL, so the effect is not gated by the input directions each task's rollouts excite

imports.finding: bf16 storage hides sub-ulp updates, so apparent RLVR sparsity is a model-conditioned readout; RLVR runs on different data from one base share the updated-entry mask far above a Bernoulli baseline.
imports.how: Explains why Math-RL and Code-RL change the same entries 1.64x above chance while agreeing in sign only at chance, and predicts that the excess nearly vanishes within |w| deciles and that small-|w| entries register changes far more often.

imports.finding: For Olmo-3-7B RL-Zero deltas the effect sits in the signs and cross-coordinate structure, not in large weights on high-Fisher coordinates (magnitude alignment about 1; a sign-flip null loses most of the effect).
imports.how: Lets the theory predict that flattening every changed entry to one magnitude per matrix, keeping signs, recovers near-RL MATH-500 accuracy, a number no team item supplies.
